label: WooCommerce
terms_note: Tenant's own WordPress + WooCommerce site; keys generated by the store admin for a WP user (permissions follow that user); HTTPS required by our client (Basic auth in clear text refused); no platform rate limit (host-dependent); open-source (GPL), no fees beyond hosting / payments.

discovery.auth: api_key (REST API consumer key + secret generated under WooCommerce › Settings › Advanced › REST API for a chosen WP user with read/write; HTTP Basic over HTTPS or OAuth 1.0a one-legged)
sdks: official REST API client libraries (JS / PHP / Python / Ruby) on developer.woocommerce.com

reference.verdict: **Verdict** — has_api: **yes**.Confidence: **high** — official developer documentation opened by the auditor.
auth: 1. Store admin: WooCommerce › Settings › Advanced › REST API › Add key (user, read/write) → consumer key + secret (shown once).
2. Paste both into the channel vault; client uses HTTPS Basic auth.

endpoints.call: order meta / notes (or Shipment Tracking extension endpoint)

reference.limits: None built into WooCommerce; host / WAF dependent (client maps 429 → RateLimited, 30 s). - Open-source store owned by the tenant; API keys inherit the WP user's capabilities.
mcp_sdk: SDK: official REST API client libraries (JS / PHP / Python / Ruby) on developer.woocommerce.com

fields.name: consumer_key
fields.help: WooCommerce REST API consumer key (WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API > Add key, Read/Write) sent as the HTTP Basic username over HTTPS.

fields.name: consumer_secret
fields.help: The consumer secret shown once when the key is created; sent as the HTTP Basic password.

config_fields.name: store_host
config_fields.help: Host (and any path prefix) of the merchant's WooCommerce store without scheme, e.g. shop.example.com or example.com/shop; every call goes to https://<store_host>/wp-json/wc/v3/... (HTTPS only: Basic auth with the consumer key/secret is documented for HTTPS; plain-HTTP stores need OAuth 1.0a, not supported).

me.note: GET /wp-json/wc/v3/system_status (manage_woocommerce capability) returns the store's environment {home_url, site_url, version, wp_version, ...}, database, active_plugins, theme and settings; it verifies the key pair and identifies the store.

create_listing.note: POST /wp-json/wc/v3/products creates a simple product: name, type=simple, regular_price (sent as the documented decimal string, e.g. "21.99"), description, sku, stock_quantity and manage_stock=true (so stock_quantity takes effect); the response is the product {id, permalink, status (publish by default), ...}. `currency` is the store's currency (not per product) and `image_urls` need images[{src}] objects, so both are ignored.

update_listing.note: PUT /wp-json/wc/v3/products/{id} with only the given fields (name, regular_price as the documented decimal string, description, stock_quantity); stock_quantity only applies when the product has manage_stock on (see set_inventory). Returns the product; `status` is the product status (publish/draft/...).

end_listing.note: Unpublishes the product by setting status=draft (reversible; the product keeps its data). DELETE /products/{id} (trash, or force=true to delete permanently) is not used.

set_inventory.note: PUT /wp-json/wc/v3/products/{id} {manage_stock: true, stock_quantity} sets product-level stock. `listing_id` (the product id) is required: the endpoint is addressed by id, and a lookup by `sku` (GET /products?sku=) would be a second call the runtime does not chain. Variation stock is per variation (PUT /products/{id}/variations/{vid}, not mapped).

list_orders.note: GET /wp-json/wc/v3/orders?page&per_page(max 100)&status(any|pending|processing|on-hold|completed|cancelled|refunded|failed|trash)&after(ISO8601). Returns an array of orders; `total` is a decimal string ("29.35") as WooCommerce returns it; the total count is only in the X-WP-Total header, so `total` of the page is null.

mark_shipped.note: PUT /wp-json/wc/v3/orders/{id} {status: completed} (WooCommerce's fulfilled state). Core WooCommerce has no tracking fields: `carrier` and `tracking_number` are NOT recorded (they would need meta_data [{key, value}] objects or the Shipment Tracking extension's wc-shipment-tracking/v3 endpoint, neither expressible here).

not_offered.listing_metrics: No per-product analytics endpoint: GET /wp-json/wc/v3/reports/* are store-wide sales / top-sellers reports, not views or conversions for one listing.

evidence: host woocommerce.com: DNS ok, TLSv1.3 (Let's Encrypt)
